title: Cut in a wall above a skirting board with a paint edger, keeping its guide wheels on the board's top edge
instruction: The paint edger's pad is loaded. Paint the wall along the skirting board between the two green tabs: run the edger with its pad flat on the wall and its wheels on the board's top edge, then stand it back in its rest.
context: Repainting a room starts with cutting in: a clean band of new paint along the skirting boards, door casings and ceiling, before the open wall is rolled. Most people who have painted a room have done it. A paint edger makes it easier: a flat paint pad with two small guide wheels along one edge. Run along the top of the skirting board, the wheels hold the pad's edge just clear of the board while the pad, kept flat and pressed lightly on the wall, paints right down to it. Let the wheels ride up and a bare strip is left above the board; let the pad tip or drop and it smears paint on the board, which then has to be wiped and repainted.
setup:
Millimetres. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left (+) or right (-) of the midline, z up from the table top; arm bases at y = +305 and -305. One fixed layout; the edger is the only loose object.
1) Wall section, fixed: 1/2 in (12.7) gypsum drywall, 380 long (y = -60 to +320) and 200 tall, painted a pale warm grey (the old colour), its face the plane x = 250 toward the robot, screwed to a pine (wood) 2x4 (38 x 89) frame behind it; the frame is fixed to the table.
2) Skirting board, fixed: primed MDF square-edge baseboard, 11/16 x 3-1/2 in (17.5 x 89), white semi-gloss, nailed along the wall's foot for its full length: face at x = 232.5, flat top 17.5 deep at z = 89. Two green painter's-tape tabs, 15 wide and 25 tall, on its face at the top, inner edges at y = 0 and y = +300, mark the stretch to paint.
3) Paint edger, loose: Shur-Line Edger Pro (item 2006561). Red polypropylene (plastic) head carrying a 4-3/4 x 3-3/4 in (121 x 95) refill pad (white synthetic fabric pile on a stiff plastic backing, 4 thick) loaded with mid-blue latex wall paint. Two black plastic guide wheels, 14 across, axles normal to the pad, at the corners of the head's lower long edge, 103 apart, hold the pad's lower edge 1.5 above the surface they roll on; their rims run 6.5 to 11.5 behind the pad's face. A black plastic palm grip on the head's back, 58 across its flats over its upper 40 and 38 deep, turns on a swivel about the axis normal to the pad (free, stops at 90 degrees each way). About 100 g with the paint. Grip, wheel and swivel sizes are scaled from the maker's photos to the listed pad size.
4) Edger rest, fixed (made for the trial): grey-painted 12 plywood (wood) base, 85 x 160 (x = 177 to 262, y = +335 to +495), 3 lower under the pad, with a pine ledge 32 x 80, 19 tall (x = 182 to 214) under the grip's lower end.
Start: the edger stands in the rest on both wheels with the grip's lower end on the ledge, pad facing the wall (+x) and touching nothing, the pad face's centre at x = 237, y = +415, 61 above the table. Both grippers open at the ready pose. Nothing else is on the table.
Scoring grid: the wall's face and the board's top and face carry a 5 mm grid (not drawn).
Friction (estimates): wet pad on painted drywall 0.40 static / 0.35 dynamic; guide wheels on the board 0.05 (they turn freely); grip 0.6 / 0.5; board 0.30 / 0.25; rest 0.5 / 0.4.
scoring:
Read at the end on the 5 mm grid (real trial: a square-on photo through a 5 mm grid transparency); a cell is painted when at least half of it carries the new paint. Band: the wall from the board's top (89 above the table) to 40 above it, between the tabs' inner edges (y = 0 to 300): 8 rows x 60 = 480 cells. Cut line: the band's lowest row (89 to 94), 60 cells. Trim paint: new paint on any cell of the board's top or face (real trial: any mark 2 or more across). In its rest: the edger stands on both wheels on the rest's base (each wheel's bottom from 4 below to 3 above the base's top), the pad face's centre from 10 behind to 8 in front of and within 30 either side of its start, the pad facing the wall within 15 degrees and the grip upright within 8 degrees; released (every gripper TCP at least 30 from the edger's bounding box) and still (under 10 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s, the swivel under 0.05 rad/s).
1.0: at least 95% of band cells and 95% of cut-line cells painted, no trim paint, and the edger in its rest, released and still, for the last 1 s.
0.75: the same paint and no trim paint, but the edger not in its rest (still held, moving, or put down anywhere else).
0.5: at least 80% of band cells and 80% of cut-line cells painted, no trim paint.
0.25: at least 40% of band cells painted, with or without trim paint (any trim paint limits the score to 0.25).
0: anything else, including an edger that never paints the wall.
Sticky 0 for the rest of the trial: the pad touches the table (any pad corner within 1 of the table top) or the edger falls off the table. Paint on the wall above the band or beyond the tabs costs nothing. Success is 1.0.
reset_notes: Use zero object jitter. Wipe the new paint off the wall and the board with a damp cloth before it dries (or swap in a freshly painted wall panel); fit a fresh pad and load it from the edger tray; stand the edger back in its rest on both wheels, the grip's lower end on the ledge, pad toward the wall. Wall, board and rest stay fixed to the table.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The pad's pile does not deform: a rigid plate stands in for it, and a cell is painted when it lies within the pad's outline (plus 0.5) and no more than 2 in front of its face, the pile's reach (its give is a tolerance here, not the skill). Paint load, drips and thin spots are not modelled. The guide wheels are low-friction rims that do not turn. Grip shape, wheel size and offset, swivel range, mass and frictions are estimates.
